title: Two Sum
description:
Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target.

You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.

You can return the answer in any order.

examples.explanation: nums[0] + nums[1] = 2 + 7 = 9, so the answer is [0,1].

hints: A brute force approach checks every pair of numbers in O(n²) time.
For each number, calculate target - currentNumber.
Store previously seen numbers in a HashMap for O(1) lookup.
Check for the complement before inserting the current element.
intuition: For every number x, we need another number target - x. Instead of searching the remaining array every time, store previously seen numbers in a HashMap. If the complement already exists, we have found the answer immediately.

patternExplanation.name: Complement Lookup using HashMap
patternExplanation.coreIdea: Store visited elements and check whether the required complement already exists.

bruteForce.reason: Every element is compared with every other element.

optimal.reason: Each element is processed once and HashMap operations take O(1) on average.

approaches.name: Brute Force
HashMap (Optimal)

edgeCases.reason: Duplicate values can form the answer.
The HashMap solution works regardless of sign.
Array size can be as small as 2.

pitfalls: Adding the current element before checking its complement.
followUpQuestions: Can you solve it in less than O(n²) time?
What if the array is sorted?
Can you solve it with O(1) extra space?
How would you return all valid pairs?
How would you handle a stream of incoming numbers?

notes.title: HashMap Pattern
notes.description: Store numbers seen so far and check whether the complement exists.

notes.title: Why O(n) Works
notes.description: Each element is processed once and every lookup is O(1) on average.

notes.title: Common Mistake
notes.description: Insert the current element only after checking for the complement.
